title: Karmic tail 9-9-18 in the destiny matrix: “The Wizard”, a cell of knowledge and a road by moonlight

seo.title: Karmic tail 9-9-18 “The Wizard” in the destiny matrix
seo.description: 9-9-18 is the only one of 26 tails with the Moon at the root: a road to walk, not a fear to beat. A ten-second date check, why kids get it more, and eight practices.

short: In popular readings of the destiny matrix, the 9-9-18 tail is called “the Wizard” or “Magical Knowledge”, less often “the Magician”. There is less sorcery in it than the name promises. What it does have is a script that many people recognise from the first lines. The entry is the Hermit (9): faced with something unclear, a person first steps aside to work it out alone. The mechanism is the Hermit again: the working-out never ends, preparation becomes a way of life, knowledge piles up and never comes out. The root is the Moon (18): a road into the unknown that has to be walked by reflected light, without ever getting full clarity, together with your own imagination, instincts and fears. 9-9-18 is the only one of the 26 tails with the Moon at the root. Here it is not an obstacle to overcome but a place to reach. The tail appears for only one sum of the birth-date numbers — exactly 18 — and then the centre of the chart is always held by a third Hermit. So the main question of this tail is not “how do I stop being afraid” but how to leave the cell without waiting for dawn and walk by the light you already have.

sections.h2: Do you have the 9-9-18 tail? A ten-second check
paragraphs: To recognise this tail, you only need to add up three numbers from your birth date. No calculator needed.

ol: **Day arcanum** — the day you were born. If it is over 22, add its digits: 25 → 7, 29 → 11, 30 → 3, 31 → 4.
**Year arcanum** — the sum of the digits of the year. If the result is over 22, add the digits again: 1985 → 23 → 5, 1989 → 27 → 9.

paragraphs: Add the three numbers. If you get **exactly 18**, you have 9-9-18. Any other sum gives a different tail: only 18 leads to 9-9-18.

ul: 14.07.1995: 14 + 7 + 6 = 27 → not this one. This is 18-9-9: the same numbers, but the Moon stands at the entry, not at the root.
01.06.2000: 1 + 6 + 2 = 9 → not this one. This is 9-18-9: the Moon in the middle.

paragraphs: With a ready chart it is even faster: look at the bottom corner, point D, the “karmic task”. If it holds 18, your tail is 9-9-18. No other tail puts the Moon in the bottom corner.
And some people don’t need to count at all. **You definitely do not have 9-9-18** if you:

ul: were born on the 16th, 17th, 18th, 19th, 20th, 21st or 22nd of any month. Even with January and the smallest year arcanum, the sum goes over 18. The 15th has given this tail only once since 1900 — on 15 January 2000;

were born in a year whose arcanum is between 17 and 22. Since 1900 there have been 51 such years, among them 1970–1975, 1980–1984 and 1990–1993. Not a single person with 9-9-18 was born in those years. The next such year will not come until 2069.

paragraphs: Why it works. The sum 18 is not over 22, so it is not reduced: the bottom corner D is simply 18, the Moon. The centre E is the same sum plus the corner: 18 + 18 = 36 → 9, the Hermit. After that there are no options: the entry M = D + E = 18 + 9 = 27 → 9, the middle N = D + M = 18 + 9 = 27 → 9. This was checked by going through all 73,414 dates from 1900 to 2100.
Read the diagram from top to bottom, from the centre to the corner:

head: Point
Arcanum
How it is derived
rows: sum exactly 18 (bottom corner of the chart)

paragraphs: Sums that are multiples of nine give three different tails from the same numbers. They differ in where the Moon stands:
The arithmetic of the tail also points to things that popular readings keep quiet about.

ul: **This is a tail of children more than of grandmothers.** Since 1900, 9-9-18 has come up in 2% of dates — roughly one in fifty. That puts it 17th out of 26. But since the 1930s its share has grown almost without a break and has risen more than fourteenfold:

paragraphs: Among people born in the 20th century, 9-9-18 occurs in one person in 76. Among those born from 2000 to 2025 it is one in 22, and there the tail climbs to 11th place. The reason is arithmetic. For the sum to come out at exactly 18, the year arcanum has to be small: the day and the month together give at least 2. Many 20th-century years have an arcanum from 17 to 22, and the tail becomes impossible. Years of the 21st century have an arcanum from 2 to 12, and 9-9-18 is possible in any of them. The most such dates — 21 each — fell in 2002, 2011 and 2020, whose year arcanum is 4.

ul: **This is a tail of the start of the year.** The month number goes into the sum, and the sum has to stay small. So among people born in January, 3.1% have 9-9-18, and among those born in December, 0.5% — almost seven times fewer. In 2026 the last date with this tail was 1 July; there will be no more before the end of the year.

**It is unique on two counts at once.** Of the 26 tails, only here is the Moon the root. In the others it opens the script (18-9-9, 18-6-6, 18-3-12, 18-6-15) or works as the mechanism (9-18-9). And only here does the Hermit hold both the entry and the middle.

sections.h2: Why “the Wizard”: the name, the legends and what they share
paragraphs: In popular lists of karmic tails, 9-9-18 is called “the Wizard”, “Magical Knowledge” or “the Magician”. Some sites also call 18-9-9 “the Wizard”: the two tails have the same numbers, and they are often mixed up.
The past life of people with this tail is told in different ways, but each time it is a story about knowledge.

ul: **The black magician.** The person had magic and used it to do harm: love spells, spells to turn people away, power over someone else’s will. Hence the advice of many readings: if you are drawn to esoteric things, use your knowledge only for good.
**The scientist in the laboratory.** A brilliant mind living alone among its experiments came, over time, to serve its own gain.

**The keeper of exclusive knowledge.** The person knew what others did not and would not share it, afraid of losing importance. Hence the “intellectual vanity” attributed to the tail: condescension towards those who know less.

**The one who feared their own gift.** The quietest version. The person gained access to secret knowledge and used it, but one day “something went wrong”. They got scared of their own abilities, put a “block” on them and lived out their life as a hermit, passing nothing on to anyone.

paragraphs: Whether these lives happened, a birth date cannot say: numbers and cards are silent about the past. But the legends themselves agree on one thing, and that one thing shows in the cards. In every version the person **has** the knowledge. The trouble is not with the knowledge but with what stands between it and people. The magician turned knowledge against people, the scientist towards himself, the keeper hid it from people, and the frightened one hid it from himself. No wonder some readings treat harmful magic and a flat denial of everything “magical” as equally dangerous: they are two ways of mishandling the same gift.

The name also has a footing in the cards themselves. Back in 1910, Waite mentioned interpretations in which the Hermit’s lantern holds “the Light of Occult Science” and his staff is “a Magic Wand”. He granted that they were “true after their own manner”, but thought they missed the main thing. In his divinatory list, the Moon has, among other things, “occult forces”, next to “darkness”, “terror”, “deception” and “error”. For Benebell Wen, the Moon is “the signifier for society’s magi, priest, or shaman”, and the card itself is “the beginning manifestation into consciousness” of esoteric knowledge.

Another thought of Wen’s comes even closer to the legend. The Moon, she says, speaks of **hidden abilities**: a person with “hidden abilities to harness both tame elements and wild elements”. And of **resistance**: what lies in the unconscious rises into the conscious, and the person resists it “due to fear or hyperactive defense mechanisms”. That is almost word for word the legend of the frightened wizard. The gift is there, the fear of it is there, and there is a defence that keeps the gift from coming out.

Our reading of the name. The “Wizard” of this tail is not someone who casts spells. It is someone who has a lunar gift — imagination, instinct, the ability to see what is hidden — and keeps it locked in a tower of books and reflection. The tower is the two Hermits that stand in front of the Moon. The legendary “block” is them.

sections.h2: Two lights: the lantern and the moon
paragraphs: To understand 9-9-18, it helps to put side by side the two sources of light on its cards.

The Hermit has a lantern. This is his own light: bright, close, obedient. It lights a circle a few steps wide, and inside that circle everything is visible. Wen reads the Hermit’s lantern in two ways: as a light for those walking in darkness, and as the gaze of someone who “sees the world through his or her own light” and follows only their own thoughts. In this tail, the second reading is at work.

The Moon’s light is reflected. It is dim, borrowed and beyond control, but it lights the whole landscape: the water, the road between the towers, the mountains on the horizon. Nothing is sharp, but you can see where to go. Waite says it plainly: “The intellectual light is a reflection and beyond it is the unknown mystery which it cannot shew forth.” And Wen suggests that the very first clarity a person receives comes from the moon, that is, from a reflection, “rather than from the sun itself”.

A person with 9-9-18 trusts only the lantern. Until they have found the answer themselves and checked it all the way through, they cannot take a step. But the road the tail’s root points to is one the lantern cannot light at all. Waite calls the path between the Moon’s towers “the issue into the unknown”. The dog and the wolf by this road are “the fears of the natural mind in the presence of that place of exit, when there is only reflected light to guide it”. No other light ever falls on it. You can stand at its start as long as you like and read more and more books — it will not get any brighter.

This metaphor has a basis in physiology, and it explains the tail better than many words. The eye does not adjust to the dark at once. After 5–10 minutes night vision gets noticeably better, and the eye reaches full sensitivity after about forty minutes. Bright light knocks this adjustment out. That is why astronomers use dim red torches when observing: the retinal cells responsible for night vision are almost blind to red light.

Someone holding a bright lantern in front of their eyes sees almost nothing beyond its circle. It is not that the night is so dark: their eyes are tuned to the lantern. **The brighter the light in your hand, the blacker the night around you.** This is the mechanism of 9-9-18. The longer a person works things out alone, the scarier everything beyond what they understand looks — and the more they need to work things out further. But dim the lantern and wait, and the road, the trees and the horizon emerge from the dark. Moonlight, it turns out, is enough.

The task of the tail is not to throw the lantern away. With three Hermits in the chart that is neither possible nor necessary: depth and independent thinking are these people’s real gift. The task is to dim it enough for the eyes to get used to the moon.

For comparison, the numerical neighbours. In 18-9-9 the fog comes first and drives the person into the cell. In 9-18-9 the fog grows inside the cell itself. In 9-9-18 the cell comes first and the fog is at the end of the road. And it is not an enemy but the destination.

sections.h2: How the loop works: “I’ll work it out first” — “not ready yet” — the night nobody went out into
paragraphs: Here is how the loop can look step by step. The scene is made up as an example; everyone with this tail has their own scenery.

Vera is 36. She has been studying psychology for nine years: a second degree, eleven certificates, a shelf of books on anxiety and attachment. A friend runs a women’s club and invites her to lead a meeting: “Tell our girls about anxiety — you know more about it than anyone.”

**Entry — the Hermit: “I’ll work it out first.”** Vera says neither “yes” nor “no” but “I need to prepare”. This is not fright but a habitual first move: anything new and unclear must first be understood alone, in silence, with her own mind. The habit has paid off many times. Vera really does understand things more deeply than others, because she is not satisfied with ready-made answers. The Hermit at the entry of this tail is not running away from people. It is the conviction that you must first see everything by your own light, and only then go. **In 9-9-18 fear comes not first but last.**

**Mechanism — the Hermit again: “Not ready yet.”** Vera sits down to prepare and finds a gap: she does not know the new research well. She buys a course. The course opens three new questions. The meeting is moved to the autumn, then to “after New Year”. The circle of light moves with her, and beyond its edge it is always dark: every explanation she finds opens up the next unknown. Wen calls the Hermit the card of both “neophyte initiates and prophets”. Vera is stuck in the first role: her knowledge is already a mentor’s, but she feels like an eternal student. Waite insisted that the Hermit is **“a card of attainment … rather than a card of quest”**. His figure stands on a summit: it has already arrived.

Meanwhile, in the darkness beyond the lantern’s circle, the Moon grows by itself. Before sleep, Vera runs through the meeting in her head. Someone asks a question she cannot answer. Someone cries, and she says the wrong thing and makes it worse. A woman in the third row smirks. Sometimes she dreams the other way: the meeting goes brilliantly, Vera is invited onto the radio, she brings out a book. Both dreams are the Moon — “life of the imagination apart from life of the spirit”, as Waite calls it. The unknown does not stay empty. If nobody goes out into it, imagination moves in — both frightening and beautiful.

**Root — the Moon: the night she never went out into.** The meeting never happened. A year later Vera learns that the club invited an acquaintance with one introductory course, and she is already running her third group. Vera’s first thought: “But she doesn’t really know anything.” This is where the “intellectual vanity” of popular readings comes from. It is not arrogance but defence: someone who went out into the night with less light seems reckless. But the acquaintance walked the road, and Vera knows it from a map. The tail’s root says that the road into the unknown is only ever walked by reflected light. The dog and the wolf will howl: on the card they stand on both sides of the road, and there is no way round them.

**Repeat.** A year later Vera is asked again, and the bar is already higher: “After ten years of study I can’t give a bad talk.” Each year of preparation raises the price of the first step. The burrow gets deeper, and climbing out of it gets scarier.

**In this tail, fear is born not from what happened but from what never did.** The road not taken fills up with imagination. The longer a person stands at its start, the more monsters there are on it.

The same pattern shows up in other settings. A man has been “gathering information” for six years before changing careers. A young woman writes songs and puts them in a drawer: “I’ll post them when I’m sure of my voice.” Someone has studied tarot for fifteen years and has never once read the cards for another person — “what if I get it wrong”. A father has read twenty books on parenting and is afraid to answer his son without preparing. A man in love wants to “sort out his feelings first” — and keeps sorting them out until she marries someone else. Everywhere it is one movement: step aside to understand — understand without end — never set out on the road.

sections.h2: The Scholar, the Recluse, the Dreamer: one and the same tail
paragraphs: Legends about 9-9-18 seem to paint different people: a magician, a scientist, a keeper, a recluse. In fact these are three states of one script, and in each one a different card outweighs the rest.

head: The Scholar
The Recluse
The Dreamer
The tail lived through
rows: the Hermit in the middle and in the centre
“first I need to work it out”
“come on, I roughly know the way”
walked by whatever light there is
someone with whom it is not scary not to know
sometimes being wrong in front of people

paragraphs: **The Scholar** is the state people recognise most often. The Hermit at the entry leads here. The person knows a lot, thinks deeply and is always preparing. They are valued as an expert; people come to them for advice. But their own life stays a rough draft: decisions, projects and changes wait for the moment when everything becomes clear. Waite argued against explaining the Hermit as “a wise man in search of truth and justice”. His Hermit has already found the truth and holds up his beacon on an eminence. The Scholar of this tail knows enough to give light, but is still searching.

**The Recluse** is the state in which the second Hermit and the centre of the chart outweigh the rest. The person stops even preparing to go out: “I’m fine on my own”, “people wear me out”, “nobody will understand anyway”. Popular readings credit this tail with a difficult character, stubbornness and excessive demands on people: relationships that fall short of the ideal simply never start. Esoteric culture is quick to hand this state an excuse: “people drain your energy”, “shield yourself from other people’s vibrations”. Waite argued with this kind of Hermit. He called reading the card as “occult isolation, as the protection of personal magnetism against admixture” one of “the frivolous renderings which we owe to Éliphas Lévi”. The mysteries, in his words, “secure their own protection from those who are unprepared”, so there is no need to hide them.

**The Dreamer** is the state where the Moon sounds, but without a road. The unknown is not lived but imagined: in daydreams, fantasies and dreams, in the worlds of books and games, in esoteric systems where everything has already been explained. This is where the tail becomes “magical” in the popular sense. The person feels they have a gift, and they are right, but the gift lives only inside. Popular readings warn that with this tail “thoughts materialise”: whatever script you draw in your head will come true. Our reading is simpler. A script that has never been tested with a step gets lived through in the head for so long that the person starts behaving as if it had already come true. And then it does come true — not by magic, but because that is exactly how they behaved.

The states follow one another in a circle. Years of the Scholar end in tiredness and “oh, forget the lot of them”, and the person moves into the Recluse. In the quiet, dreams grow, and the Recluse becomes the Dreamer. Then a new interest comes along, the Dreamer sits down with the books — and is the Scholar again. One and the same person can go through all three in ten years without ever setting out on the road.

sections.h2: The hidden fourth card: everyone with 9-9-18 has the Hermit in the centre
paragraphs: The nine in the centre of this tail is not a coincidence but a rule: the sum 18 always gives a centre of 18 + 18 = 36 → 9. Everyone with 9-9-18 has the Hermit in the middle of the matrix.

The centre of the chart is read as the comfort zone — the place a person comes back to in order to recover. For 9-9-18 it is solitude, silence, a book, your own thoughts. That is why the tail rarely feels like a problem. It feels like character: “I’m an introvert”, “I need to think everything through”, “I don’t like to rush”. All of this may be true. The script begins where the comfort zone becomes the only place to live, and the road out of it is never walked.

Three Hermits in one chart are not loneliness tripled. Each has its own role. The central one is a home to come back to, and it is needed. The entry one is the habit of stepping aside to understand, and it is useful. The middle one is the habit of not coming back until you understand completely. It is this one that keeps the loop going.
And now the most curious part. The numbers of this tail move in a closed circle.

ul: **Moon + Moon = Hermit.** The centre is 18 + 18 = 36 → 9.
**Moon + Hermit = Hermit.** That is how both the entry and the middle come out: 18 + 9 = 27 → 9.
**Hermit + Hermit = Moon.** The entry and the middle together give exactly the root: 9 + 9 = 18.

paragraphs: The last one is not a formula of the method but a coincidence of numbers. What follows is our reading, not a rule. Whatever is added to the Moon in this tail, the result is the Hermit again: meeting the unknown turns into withdrawal. And two withdrawals added together give the Moon: solitude multiplied by solitude breeds fog. The loop of 9-9-18 is written right into the arithmetic. There is one way to break it — to walk through the Moon, not to add another Hermit to it.
The same four cards — three Hermits and the Moon — appear for people with 18-9-9. But their roles are the opposite.

rows: The Moon: an unclear signal, a ready-made version
The Hermit: step aside and work it out
The Hermit: the version grows stronger in silence
The Hermit: carry the light out to people
The Moon: go out into the unknown

paragraphs: In 18-9-9 a person comes out of the fog and learns to hold up the lantern for others. In 9-9-18 a person knows how to light their own way and learns to walk where their lantern is not enough.

sections.h2: Where else 9 and 18 sound in your chart
paragraphs: These people have nine and eighteen not only on the bottom ray. Below are the points that are the same in all 924 charts with 9-9-18 calculated since 1900:

head: Where in the matrix
What everyone with 9-9-18 has
rows: Bottom corner, point D — karmic task
9-9-18 — the same numbers as the tail
Sky line (month — D — their sum), middle
only 9 or 18, and at least one of them is 18

paragraphs: Some rows of the table are the same points under different names. The entry of the relationship line and the energy of Svadhisthana are point M, the entry of the tail. The energy of Muladhara, the middle of the sky line and age 60 are point D, its root. There are fewer independent matches than rows, but the table shows in which themes of the chart the tail can also be heard.

**Manipura 9-9-18: the same numbers at the centre of the energy chart.** The Manipura row is made of the centre, the centre again and their sum. For everyone with 9-9-18 it is 9, 9 and 18 — the same numbers in the same order. Hence the frequent question about “9-9-18 in the centre of the matrix”. But in Manipura this is not a tail; it is the row of status, will and money. Everyone with 18-9-9 gets it too, and together that is about one person in nine. Our reading of the row: it is easier to act once you have found the answer on your own, while uncertainty and other people’s judgement are coloured by the Moon. In the tail these cards describe a script; in Manipura, a style of action.

**Purposes: only the Hermit and the Moon.** The personal, social, spiritual and planetary purposes of people with 9-9-18 can only be 9 or 18. The reason lies in a property of nine: however many times you add up the digits, the remainder after dividing by 9 stays the same. In this tail A + B + C equals 18, D is also 18, and both divide by 9. All the purposes are built from sums of the same A, B, C and D, so they too are multiples of nine. Between 1 and 22 there are only two such numbers — 9 and 18.

head: Personal
Social
Spiritual
Planetary
Share of people with the tail

paragraphs: At least one purpose is always the Moon. The personal one splits almost exactly in half: half the people with this tail have the Hermit, the other half the Moon. What follows is our conclusion; it is not in the books. These people have the Hermit and the Moon both in the karmic task and in the purpose. The tail is not someone else’s burden but the same clay the purpose is made of, only not yet fired.

**Svadhisthana with the Hermit, Muladhara with the Moon.** For everyone with 9-9-18, the energy of the row of joy and creativity comes from the Hermit: joy comes in long pursuits where nobody hurries you and you can get to the heart of things. The energy of the row of body and support comes from the Moon. Our reading: these people have to build stability not on full clarity but on the ability to stand on their own feet when there is no clarity. Until they have that ability, any uncertainty — a puzzling bill, a rumour of changes at work — feels as if the ground is slipping away.

**The Hermit at the entrance to love.** Point M starts not only the tail but also the relationship line M–R1–R. So for everyone with 9-9-18, closeness is opened by the Hermit: take a good look, understand yourself, don’t rush. More on this in the section on relationships.

**A triple mirror for those born in 1989, 1998, 2007, 2016 and 2025.** If you have 9-9-18 and were born in a year with arcanum 9, all three permutations of these numbers stand in your chart. The tail is 9-9-18. The relationship line is 9-18-9. The money line is 18-9-9. On top of that, the Svadhisthana row is 18-9-9, the Muladhara row is 9-18-9, and Manipura, as for everyone with this tail, is 9-9-18. Since 1900 there have been 70 such dates, for example 05.04.1989 and 05.04.1998. Of these, only the bottom ray is the tail; on the lines and in the chakras the same numbers describe their own area and are read by its roles. Still, in such a chart one theme sounds six times, and it is hard not to hear it.

**The September coincidence.** For people with 9-9-18 born in September, the talent line on the top ray is also 9-9-18. Only the order on the ray is reversed: on the top ray the 9 stands by the outer corner and the Moon next to the centre; on the bottom one the Hermit is by the centre and the Moon at the very edge of the chart. Our reading: in the talent line the Moon is close to home — a gift for working with images and hunches from the inside. In the tail the Moon is at the end of the road, and it has to be walked through.
**The Moon at sixty.** The age scale gives the bottom corner D the years from 60 to 70, so for everyone with this tail the Moon falls on that decade. This is a rhyme, not a forecast.

sections.h2: A parable: the wise gudgeon and the wizard who broke his staff
paragraphs: The parallels below are ours, not a tradition of the method. But two stories, written long before the destiny matrix, read like a detailed map of 9-9-18: one as the tail’s shadow, the other as the way out of it.

paragraphs.h3: The gudgeon who bathed in moonlight

paragraphs: In 1883 Mikhail Saltykov-Shchedrin wrote the fairy tale “The Wise Gudgeon” (Premudry piskar). The hero’s parents lived a long life in the river and “ended up neither in the fish soup nor in the pike’s maw”. His father once nearly landed in the pot: fishermen dragged him ashore in a net, and only a chance old man let the little fish go back into the river. Dying, the father told his son: “Mind, son, … if you want to enjoy life, keep both eyes open!”

“But the young gudgeon had a whole chamber of wits.” He began “casting about with that mind” and saw danger everywhere: the pike, the crayfish, the man with a rod. His conclusion was this: “I must live so that nobody notices,” he said to himself, “or else I’m done for!” For a whole year he hollowed out a burrow with his nose — such that “he could get into it, but nobody else could squeeze in”. It came out “clean, neat — just the right size for one”.

Further on, Shchedrin has a line that is hard to read without a smile if you know the cards of this tail: “At night he took his exercise and bathed in the moonlight, and by day he climbed into his burrow and trembled.” Once a crayfish stopped in front of his burrow — “standing motionless, as if bewitched, goggling at him with its bony eyes”. In the burrow the gudgeon dreamt that he had won two hundred thousand on a lottery ticket. He never married and had no children: “No friends, no family; he went to no one, and no one came to him.” He lived “a hundred years and then some”, and towards the end “almost went blind from the eternal twilight”.
Lay the tale next to the tail.

ul: **“A whole chamber of wits” — the Hermit at the entry.** The gudgeon is not a coward by nature. He is clever and has thought everything through. His first move is not to run but to “cast about with his mind”.
**A burrow for one — the Hermit in the middle and in the centre.** A shelter made with love and skill: a year of work, “clean, neat”.

**Moonlight, the crayfish, the dream of winning, the eternal twilight — the Moon that was never walked through.** Everything on Waite’s Moon card, the gudgeon has: night, water, a creature from the depths, imagination. Only the road is missing. He bathes in the moonlight but swims nowhere by it.

**The father who nearly ended up in the soup — an inherited fear.** The gudgeon lives by someone else’s fright, bequeathed to him. In the popular tradition a karmic tail is also a script passed down by inheritance.

paragraphs: Before he dies, the gudgeon has a thought: “What if I crawl out of my burrow and swagger down the whole length of the river!” “But no sooner had he thought of it than he took fright again. And, trembling, he began to die. He lived — trembling, and he died — trembling.” And he asks himself: “What joys had he had? Whom had he comforted? To whom had he given good advice? To whom had he said a kind word? Whom had he sheltered, warmed, protected? Who had heard of him? Who would remember that he had ever existed?” There is one answer to all of them: “To no one, no one.” Other fish swim past the burrow, and not one of them takes any interest in it.

These are the Hermit’s questions. Wen calls it the card of guidance and mentorship, and the beacon of Waite’s Hermit means “where I am, you also may be”. Nobody came to the gudgeon’s burrow for advice, and he had no one to shine for. The word premudry, “most wise”, in the title is a mockery, but an accurate one. Waite, too, writes of a prudence that saves energy “because of the stress, the terror and the manifest impertinences of this life”. But Waite adds at once that “true prudence is concerned with the one thing needful”. The gudgeon saved something else — life itself. And found nothing to spend it on.

The tale is a satire on the frightened “moderately liberal” intelligentsia of the 1880s, and Shchedrin deliberately lays it on thick. It is an extreme form, not a portrait of people with 9-9-18. But the direction is recognisable.

paragraphs.h3: The wizard who broke his staff

paragraphs: The second story is brighter, and its hero is a wizard in the literal sense. In Shakespeare’s The Tempest, written around 1611, Prospero, the rightful Duke of Milan, tells his daughter how he lost power. He handed the government to his brother, and himself “to my state grew stranger, being transported / And rapt in secret studies”. “I, thus neglecting worldly ends, all dedicated / To closeness and the bettering of my mind…” “Me, poor man, my library / Was dukedom large enough.” His brother took advantage of this and seized the throne, and Prospero and his little daughter were put into a rotten boat and cast out to sea. A kind Neapolitan lord managed to put books from his library into the boat — volumes Prospero prized “above my dukedom”.

For twelve years Prospero lives on the island. He calls his dwelling a cell, like a hermit’s: “This cell’s my court.” The island is full of the lunar: spirits, dreams, illusions, a storm in which nobody actually drowns. The mother of the savage Caliban was a witch “so strong / That could control the moon”. Trinculo the jester, stumbling on Caliban, takes him for a fish: “What have we here? a man or a fish?” A creature from the water that has crawled out onto land — like the crayfish on Waite’s card. On this island Prospero speaks the most famous words of the play: “We are such stuff / As dreams are made on, and our little life / Is rounded with a sleep.” And at once he admits that his “old brain is troubled”, and goes off for a walk “to still my beating mind”. Waite ends his description of the Moon on the same note: “The face of the mind directs a calm gaze upon the unrest below”, and the words of the Gospel sound: “Peace, be still.”
Lay this story next to the tail too.

ul: **“My library was dukedom large enough” — the Hermit at the entry.** The world of people and affairs is handed over to others for the sake of books.
**Twelve years in the cell — the Hermit in the middle and in the centre.** Solitude has become both life and power: on the island Prospero runs everything himself.
**An island of dreams and spirits — the Moon.** The wizard lives in a lunar world and rules it. But he rules it from the cell, with staff and book.

paragraphs: Prospero’s way out has three steps, and each one fits 9-9-18 like a key.

The first step is to own your darkness. Of Caliban, whom he has treated as a monster all through the play, Prospero says in the finale: “this thing of darkness I / Acknowledge mine.” Wen describes the Moon as the shadow of the self, the repressed side that rises to the surface. While the shadow belongs to someone else, it is kept in a cave. Once owned, it stops being a monster.

The second step is to give up power over the unknown. “But this rough magic / I here abjure… I’ll break my staff, / Bury it certain fathoms in the earth, / And deeper than did ever plummet sound / I’ll drown my book.” The Hermit’s staff, remember, was called a magic wand in the old interpretations. Prospero does not give up knowledge; it stays with him. He gives up controlling every step.

The third step is to return to people with his own small strength. In the epilogue Prospero comes out to the audience without magic: “Now my charms are all o’erthrown, / And what strength I have’s mine own, / Which is most faint.” And he asks them not to let him “dwell / In this bare island”, but to release him. This is the lunar road. Sailing home to Milan, to the brother who betrayed him and an unknown future, with the light he has and no more.

**The gudgeon and Prospero are two endings of 9-9-18.** Both are clever, both spent years in hiding, both knew more than their neighbours. One never swam out: “he lived — trembling, and he died — trembling”. The other broke his staff and sailed home with his own “most faint” strength. The wizard of this tail is the one who one day leaves the cell.
The scenes below are made up as examples: this is how the tail can look, but it does not have to.

The Hermit at the tail’s entry also stands at the entry of the relationship line, so with 9-9-18 any closeness begins with a pause: take a good look, understand yourself, don’t rush. That is a good start, as long as it does not become the whole story. Most often the tail is recognised by four plots.

**“First I’ll figure out what I feel.”** The person is in love but in no hurry to show it. They need to work out whether it is real, whether this person suits them, whether the past will repeat itself. They read about attachment styles, reread the messages, argue with themselves. By the time clarity arrives, the other person is tired of waiting.

**A romance in the imagination.** The main events of the relationship happen in the head: conversations, quarrels, reconciliations, a future ten years ahead. The imagined partner understands you without a word; the real one does not. Popular readings credit this tail with idealisation and with turning down relationships that do not meet high standards. Our reading: the ideal is the Moon lived out in fantasy, because real closeness always happens a little in the dark.

**A step back at the threshold.** While the relationship is clear, all is well. When it moves to a new level — moving in together, meeting the parents, having a child — the road again leads into the unknown, and the Hermit does what it knows how to do: steps aside to think. Popular readings describe this tail exactly so: relationships end at the move to a new level. The partner sees coldness out of nowhere.
**Love at a distance.** Messaging, another city, a relationship “with no commitments for now”. This format suits the tail: you can be close and still stay in your cell.

Imagine: a partner suggests moving in together. The person with 9-9-18 answers “I need to think” and thinks for two weeks — alone, with a list of pros and cons, articles and sleepless nights. In the darkness beyond the lantern’s circle, pictures grow: rows over the washing-up, lost freedom, a break-up a year from now. The partner feels the distance and decides they are not wanted. The lived-through tail answers differently, and no confidence is needed for it: “I’m scared and curious. Let’s try it for six months and see how it goes for us.” This is the lunar road: walking without seeing the end, but seeing each other.

In its strong version, 9-9-18 has a rare gift for closeness. Wen links the Moon’s Water element with interpersonal relationships and advises going with your gut instinct about people. Such a person senses the other subtly, does not rush or interrogate, and knows how to be there when nothing is clear to the other person either. And once they stop waiting for full certainty, you can go a very long way with them.

The work script of 9-9-18 is the **eternal student**. The person knows their field more deeply than many, but keeps preparing: another course, another book, another year to “gain experience”. Popular readings speak of impostor syndrome in this tail. Our reading: the person feels like an impostor not because they know little, but because they compare their small circle of light with the boundless darkness around it. Someone who knows sees the limits of their knowledge better than someone who does not.

The second form is the **workshop without a sign**. The knowledge is there, but there is no way out to people. Consultations are free and only for friends, the product has been “almost ready” for three years, the price is “later, when I’m sure”. Imagine a programmer who has been building his own service for three years: flawless architecture, tests, documentation. Zero users; the launch keeps being put off until everything is ready. The lived-through version looks humbler and scarier: show a rough first version to ten people in a week and watch what they do with it. By moonlight, but on a real road.

In this tail, money comes not for knowledge but for going out with it. While the knowledge sits in the cell, it is invisible and nobody pays for it. Wen notes in the Moon card a strong theme of conservation, “rather than exploration or expansion”. That is often how money goes for 9-9-18: it is kept rather than put to work, and an investment, a move or a business of your own are put off until full clarity. The root of the tail suggests that the market, clients and an audience are that very night road. Everything on it is imprecise, and it can only be walked by the reflected light of other people’s responses.

Where the Hermit–Moon pairing works as a talent: research and analytics, especially where data are scarce and a guess is needed; psychology and psychotherapy; literature, translation, music, photography, film, design; work with dreams, images and symbols; teaching; any work that means leading people through the unclear — crises, transitions, changes. People choose a profession by interests and skills; the cards only hint at the setting in which this tail breathes more easily.

The Moon is the card of imagination, dreams and what rises from the depths. Wen calls it the card of “poetry and mystery”. That is why many people with 9-9-18 have a rich inner life: vivid dreams, images that come on their own, a feel for hidden meaning. And that is why they are often drawn to mythology, depth psychology, tarot, astrology and esoterica.

The tail does not prescribe any of these interests. But if you are drawn to them, 9-9-18 has its own test: **does this material come out?** Waite describes the creature crawling on the Moon card from the water onto land. It “strives to attain manifestation”, “but as a rule it sinks back whence it came”. A dream told to nobody, a drawing never drawn, a hunch never tested — that is the crayfish gone back into the water. For this tail, creative work is the shortest way along the lunar road: an image from the depths becomes a poem, a song, a painting, and others see it.

The same goes for esoterica. Someone who has studied tarot for fifteen years and never read the cards for another person lives in the Scholar. Someone who sees signs in everything and is afraid to leave the house without the right spread lives in the Dreamer. Waite warns that the Moon is “life of the imagination apart from life of the spirit”. The main risk of this tail is to mistake imagination for revelation. An insight that frightens and isolates (“someone has put the evil eye on you”, “enemies all around”, “you can’t trust anyone”) is fog. An insight that helps you go out to people and take a step is moonlight.
This is the tail of the younger generation: among those born since 2000, one child in 22 has it. In a class of thirty, there is on average more than one such pupil.

Such children often look like explorers and dreamers at once. They need to watch first before joining a game. They ask “what if…” questions, are a little afraid of the dark and of anything new, and invent worlds. None of this is a problem; it is the material of the tail.

ul: **Try before you understand.** Don’t explain the world in advance down to the last detail. Say more often: “I don’t know. Let’s try it and see.”
**Praise the step, not just the knowledge.** If a child is praised mostly for being clever and knowing everything, they will learn not to go where they might not know.
**Let the imagination out.** Draw dreams, tell made-up stories, put on home theatre. An image that has come out stops being frightening.

**Check fears together.** Don’t brush them off (“nonsense, go to sleep”) and don’t blow them up. And sometimes turn off the light in the room and sit together until your eyes adjust: the wardrobe, the chair and the window will appear by themselves. This is the tail’s main lesson in its children’s version.
**Solitude with a way back.** A child with three Hermits in the chart needs time alone. Don’t take it away, but ask afterwards: “What did you come up with in there? Will you show me?”

paragraphs.h3: If someone close to you has 9-9-18

ul: **Don’t rush them, but ask about timing.** The Hermit needs time. A good question is not “So, have you decided?” but “When would suit you to come back to this conversation?”
**Offer small steps instead of big decisions.** “Let’s just go and have a look”, not “let’s move”.
**Walk alongside.** A night road is easier to walk with two.
**Don’t mock their fears and fantasies.** Ask about them. Imagination that has been named loses half its power.
**Value the unfinished.** “Show me as it is, I’m interested” — for a person with this tail, that is an invitation onto the road.

sections.h2: Preparation or hiding, intuition or fantasy: how to tell them apart
paragraphs: Depth and preparation, solitude and intuition are strengths in themselves. They turn into a script without anyone noticing, and from the outside the difference cannot be seen. The answers to the questions below give it away.
**Preparation or hiding (the Hermit at the entry and in the middle).**

ul: Does your preparation have an end date?
What has changed over the past year: have you come closer to going out — or has the bar of “readiness” gone up?
How would you feel if tomorrow someone told you: “You already know enough”? Relief or fear?

paragraphs: **Solitude or a burrow (the Hermit in the centre).** For Wen, turning inward comes in two kinds: the Hermit turns inward to seek understanding, while the figure in the Four of Cups turns away from the world after a disappointment and may be “licking wounds”.

ul: Do you come back from the quiet with something for others — a thought, a piece of work, a word?
Do the people close to you know where you are and when you will be back?
Does silence fill you up, or do you hide in it?

paragraphs: **Intuition or fantasy (the Moon).**

ul: Is your hunch about what is happening, or about what will happen if you go out?
Have you ever tested it with a step?
Does it suggest how to go, or explain why you can’t? Intuition usually does the first, fantasy the second.

paragraphs: **Mystery or fear (the legend of the tail).** According to Waite, real mysteries “secure their own protection from those who are unprepared”.

ul: Do you keep your knowledge to yourself because it will not be understood, or because you are afraid it will be judged?
If everything you know became public tomorrow, what would you lose?

paragraphs: **Prudence or trembling (the parable of the gudgeon).**

ul: What does your caution protect — something important, or just the chance to do nothing?
If you lived to a hundred the way you live now, which of the gudgeon’s questions would you have an answer to?

sections.h2: What to do with the 9-9-18 tail: eight practices
paragraphs: The exercises below are ours; they are derived from the roles of the three cards. This is not a ritual and not a guarantee.

ol: **Dim the lantern.** When an unclear question comes up, give yourself half an hour without looking for answers: no books, articles, advice or internet. Just stay with “I don’t know” and write down what emerges: first guesses, images, sensations in the body, memories. The eyes need time to get used to the dark. So do imagination and intuition, and they do not come while the bright light of analysis is on.

**An “enough” threshold.** Before you start preparing, write down after what point you will begin: “After this course I lead my first meeting”, “When I have three reviews, I set a price”. And set a date. The Hermit will always find one more gap; let the threshold decide for it. Waite reminds us: this is a card of attainment, not of quest.

**A step for every book.** For every course, book or long article you finish — one action in the outside world: apply it, tell someone, offer it, try it. Knowledge without a step makes the lantern brighter and the night around it blacker.

**Name the dog and the wolf.** Waite calls the dog and the wolf by the lunar road the fears before going out into the unknown. Name your two as precisely as you can, for example “I’m afraid I won’t cope” and “I’m afraid they’ll laugh at me”. For each, write down what you will do if it happens. On the card the road runs between them, not around. A fear with a name howls but does not bite.

**A twilight diary.** Write down dreams, images, chance hunches, sudden ideas. Once a week, do something visible with one entry: a drawing, a poem, a short text, a conversation. Waite’s crayfish “as a rule” sinks back into the depths. Your task is to break that rule regularly.

**A premonition log.** Before taking a frightening step, write down your forecast: “he’ll say no”, “they won’t understand me”, “it’ll be a flop”. After the step, write down what actually happened. After a month, count how many night-time forecasts came true. This is how intuition is separated from fantasy — not by arguing with yourself, but by facts.

**A fellow traveller.** For a new venture, find someone who has already walked this road: a mentor, a colleague, a group. For Wen, the Hermit is not only the one who gives light to others but also the one who should accept the advice of someone wiser. The blind spot of this tail is the belief that every road must first be understood on your own.

**A walk at dusk.** Once a week, go out after sunset to a familiar, safe place — a park, a courtyard, an embankment — and don’t switch on your phone’s torch. After twenty to thirty minutes, notice how much more you can see. This is the bodily lesson of the whole tail: beyond the lantern’s circle the darkness looks thicker than it really is.

paragraphs: Five swaps for the minutes when the loop has already started turning:

ul: Instead of “I’ll work it out first” — “I’ll start and work it out as I go”.
Instead of “I’m not ready yet” — “I’m ready enough to try”.
Instead of “what if…” — “let’s see what happens”.
Instead of “I’m fine on my own” — “will you come with me?”
Instead of “someday” — “on Thursday”.

paragraphs: The practices are meant for ordinary indecision. If fear, anxiety or solitude get in the way of sleeping, working and living, if for years you cannot bring yourself to take a single step, that is something to take to a psychologist or psychotherapist. Here the matrix can only help with words for that conversation.

sections.h2: The strength of 9-9-18: a guide on the night road
paragraphs: In its lived-through version the tail gives a rare combination. The Hermit at the entry gives depth: such a person gets to the heart of things rather than settling for a ready answer. The Hermit in the middle gives stamina: they can work alone for a long time, without noise or approval. The Hermit in the centre gives an inner home to come back to. And the Moon at the root, once walked through, gives what many clever people lack: the ability to act without full clarity, a feel for what is hidden, and an imagination that creates rather than frightens.

Wen reads the Moon as a stage after transformation: the person has gone through “a personal metamorphosis” and now possesses “the intuition and premonition needed to alter his or her own fate for the better”. And on Waite’s card the Moon is waxing: its light is growing.

Waite’s Hermit has a line that takes on a new meaning in this tail. His beacon says: “where I am, you also may be.” Only someone who knows the road can say that. A person who has spent their whole life sitting on the summit can give light, but cannot lead the way. A person who has walked the lunar road — with fear, to the howling of the dog and the wolf, by reflected light — knows where the potholes are and where it is safe to walk. **The lived-through 9-9-18 is not a sage in a tower but a guide on the night road.** With them, it is not scary not to know.

Such people are good where the maps of the ground have not yet been drawn: in science at the edge of the known, in creative work, in therapy, in crises and transitions, in any work where the first step has to be taken before it gets light. The books stay with them, and so does the lantern. It is just that now they walk the road with it and know that it is lit not only by their own light.

The numbers are the same, but the Moon plays its own role in each tail, and in 9-18-9 even the centre of the chart changes. Which of the three is yours is decided by the sum of the three numbers of your date.

rows: step aside to work it out → prepare without end → go out into the unknown
unclear signal → the version grows stronger in silence → carry the light out to people
withdraw → the fog grows in silence → carry the meaning out

paragraphs: In short: in 18-9-9 the fog drives you into the cell, in 9-18-9 the fog grows in the cell, and in 9-9-18 the fog is the place you have to go out into from the cell.

sections.h2: What this reading is based on

ul: **Calculation** — the classic destiny matrix scheme with points A–T: D = A + B + C, E = A + B + C + D, M = D + E, N = D + M. The relationship line M–R1–R, where L = C + E, R = M + L, R1 = M + R. The money line L–R2–R, where R2 = L + R. The talent line B–P–K, where K = B + E, P = B + K. Rows of the energy chart: Manipura E–E, Svadhisthana L–M, Muladhara C–D, with the third column the reduced sum of the first two. The age scale gives point D the decade of 60–70 years. Every sum over 22 is reduced by adding its digits. The frequencies by generation, year and month and the constant points of the chart were obtained by going through all 46,298 dates from 1 January 1900 to 4 October 2026, and for each date the calculation was checked against the calculator’s engine. The “sum exactly 18” condition, the constant centre 9 and the absence of the tail under the “minus 22” rule were checked on all 73,414 dates from 1900 to 2100.

**Card meanings** — A. E. Waite, The Pictorial Key to the Tarot (1910, reissued 1922) and Benebell Wen, Holistic Tarot (2015). Quotations are given in the original English. Waite’s divinatory meanings are taken from Part III of his book. Waite retells the readings of the lantern as “the Light of Occult Science” and the staff as “a Magic Wand” in Part I, which is also where his reflection on prudence appears. Wen’s words on hidden abilities, resistance and conservation belong to her description of the Moon in a tarot spread, not to a number calculated from a date.

**Parables** — M. E. Saltykov-Shchedrin, “The Wise Gudgeon” (1883), from the Collected Works in 20 volumes, vol. 16, book 1; quotations in our translation. W. Shakespeare, The Tempest (c. 1611), quoted in the original. The parallels between both stories and the tail are ours.
**Dark adaptation** — M. Kalloniatis, C. Luu, Light and Dark Adaptation (Webvision). Applying it to the tail is a metaphor, not a physiological trait of people with 9-9-18.

**The names “the Wizard”, “Magical Knowledge” and “the Magician” and the past-life legends** come from popular interpretations of the destiny matrix. Neither Waite nor Wen wrote about the matrix or karmic tails. Assembling the three cards into a script, the “two lights”, the arithmetic loop, the states of the Scholar, the Recluse and the Dreamer, and the practices are the author’s interpretation.

The destiny matrix has no scientific evidence base. This reading is a tool for reflecting on yourself, not a prediction, not a diagnosis and not advice on what to do about health, money or loved ones.

paragraphs: In compatibility, 9-9-18 can be read as the task of giving feelings a clear voice within a quiet relationship. The Hermit at M concerns the wish for personal space; the Hermit at N develops the task through the habit of processing experiences alone; the Moon at D focuses on unspoken feelings and guesses that replace conversation. This is our editorial synthesis using Lisovskaya’s pair roles. The nines describe a wish and a way of seeking an answer, rather than “double coldness.”

One person may come home upset and want to think things through first. The other asks no questions but notices brief replies and withdraws too. Both may be trying to protect each other, while each sees only distance. The middle nine helps find accurate words if reflection eventually leads to a conversation. When reflection remains the only way to cope, the Moon’s task emerges in the stories each person invents about the other’s silence.

A brief sentence before taking time alone can help: “I’m upset about something at work. I need an hour; I’ll tell you after dinner.” The other can explain what they had begun to assume and ask for clarification without presenting a guess as fact. The difficulty is demanding immediate openness or endlessly postponing a promised conversation. A definite time to reconnect preserves personal space while giving feelings a way to be expressed without watchfulness and accidental hurt.

faq.q: What happened in the past life of a person with the 9-9-18 tail?
faq.a: Popular interpretations tell several legends. Most often it is about harmful magic: love spells, spells to turn people away, power over someone else’s will. There are versions about a reclusive scientist who turned his mind to his own gain; about a keeper of exclusive knowledge who would not share it for fear of losing importance; about a person who was frightened of their own gift, put a “block” on it and lived their life as a hermit. None of these stories can be checked: a birth date tells you nothing about the past. But as metaphors they are accurate. In all of them the knowledge is there, and between it and people stand fear, pride or solitude — and that can be seen in this life too, without any incarnations.

faq.q: Is 9-9-18 black magic? Do I need to take up esoterica?
faq.a: No and no. The tail is a sum of the numbers of a date; it is neither a punishment for sorcery nor a calling to it. The “magic” of this combination is the lunar gift: imagination, intuition, the ability to see what is hidden and to work with images. It is just as useful in science, art, psychology and close relationships. If esoterica still draws you, ask yourself one thing: after your practice, do you go out to people and take steps more often — or less? Knowledge that frightens and isolates is not a gift but fog.

faq.q: Why “the Magician” and “the Wizard” if the Magician arcanum is not in the tail?
faq.a: The first arcanum, the Magician, really does not occur in 9-9-18. The name came from the images of the other two cards. Benebell Wen calls the Moon “the signifier for society’s magi, priest, or shaman”, and Waite’s divinatory list gives it “occult forces”. In old interpretations the Hermit’s lantern was said to contain “the Light of Occult Science” and his staff to be “a Magic Wand”; Waite retold these readings, though he thought they missed the main thing. The “Wizard” of this tail is not someone who casts spells but someone who keeps a lunar gift locked in a tower of knowledge.

faq.q: One site says I have 9-9-18, another says 18-9-9. Which tail is mine?
faq.a: This happens because the triple is written in different orders. In the classic notation the tail is read from the centre to the bottom corner: M–N–D. Some sites write it from the corner to the centre, and then 9-9-18 turns into 18-9-9 — which is a completely different tail with different roles. The check is simple: add the day arcanum, the month and the year arcanum. Exactly 18 — you have 9-9-18. 27, 36, 45 or 54 — 18-9-9. Exactly 9 — 9-18-9. It is even simpler to look at the bottom corner of the chart: the Moon (18) stands there only for 9-9-18.

faq.q: I have 9-9-18 in the centre of the matrix, in Manipura. Is that the tail?
faq.a: No. In the energy chart the Manipura row is made of the centre, the centre again and their sum. If the centre is 9, the row is always 9-9-18. This is the case for everyone with the 9-9-18 and 18-9-9 tails — roughly one person in nine. It is the row of status, will and money, not a karmic tail, and it should be read by the roles of the row. If your tail is also 9-9-18, the match is natural: the same numbers stand at the bottom of the chart and at its centre.

faq.q: Is 9-9-18 in the relationship or money line a tail too?
faq.a: No. Only the bottom ray, read from the centre to the corner, is called the tail: M–N–D. The relationship line M–R1–R and the money line L–R2–R are other channels, and the same numbers on them are read by the roles of those channels. People who have the 9-9-18 tail never have a relationship or money line equal to 9-9-18. Such lines occur for some people with the 9-15-6, 9-12-3 and 9-3-21 tails, depending on the year of birth. And people with 9-9-18 born in 1989, 1998, 2007, 2016 or 2025 have a relationship line of 9-18-9 and a money line of 18-9-9. The talent line 9-9-18 occurs for people with the 9-9-18 and 18-9-9 tails born in September.

faq.q: Why doesn’t another calculator show 9-9-18 for me?
faq.a: There are usually two reasons. The first is the order of notation, covered in the question above. The second is the reduction rule. The classic scheme reduces a sum over 22 by adding its digits: 27 → 9. Some calculators subtract 22 instead: 27 → 5. Under that rule the 9-9-18 tail never occurs at all: even the sum 18 gives the triple 10-6-18 there. We checked every date from 1900 to 2100: under the “minus 22” rule, 9-9-18 comes out for none of them. The classic result can be checked in seconds: the sum of the day arcanum, the month and the year arcanum must be exactly 18.

faq.q: Is the 9-9-18 tail linked to fears, anxiety or health?
faq.a: Popular readings credit this tail with anxiety and psychosomatic problems, but there is no basis for that either in the cards or in the arithmetic. Waite’s Moon is imagination and the fear of the unknown — something everyone knows, not an illness. The sum of the numbers of a date cannot know how a person sleeps, what they feel or what they are ill with. If anxiety, fears or isolation get in the way of living, that is a reason to see a doctor or psychotherapist, not to reread the matrix.

faq.q: Is 9-9-18 different for women and men?
faq.a: No. Sex plays no part in the calculation: a man and a woman with the same birth date have the same chart. Popular readings write that women with this tail find it harder to trust a partner. This is a stereotype, not arithmetic: the Scholar, the Recluse and the Dreamer occur equally in everyone.

Your birth date does not change, and neither do the numbers. What changes is how you play out the script. Signs of a lived-through tail: your preparation has a deadline, and you keep to it. You show your work before it is perfect. You take steps without knowing how they will end — and your night-time forecasts come true less and less often. Imagination turns into works, not fears. You come back from solitude with something for others. And people around you are not scared not to know.

faq.q: What should I do if my child has 9-9-18?
faq.a: This is a common case: among those born since 2000, one child in 22 has 9-9-18. In 2026 the year arcanum is 10, and the tail went to children whose day arcanum and month add up to 8. There are 11 such dates, and all have passed: 7 and 25 January, 6 and 24 February, 5 and 23 March, 4 April, 3 and 30 May, 2 June, 1 July. In 2027 the year arcanum is 11, and the tail will go to those born on 6 and 24 January, 5 and 23 February, 4 and 31 March, 3 and 30 April, 2 May and 1 June. How to support such a child is covered in the section “Children with 9-9-18”. The main thing: let them try before everything has been explained, and praise the step, not just the knowledge.

a path between two towers under a waxing moon
the same for everyone with this tail: solitude is the comfort zone

report: Popular readings call the 9-9-18 tail “the Wizard”, yet the Magician is nowhere among its cards — just two Hermits and the Moon. Their past-life legends vary: a black magician with love spells, a reclusive scientist, a keeper of exclusive knowledge, someone who took fright at their own gift and put a “block” on it. None can be checked: numbers are silent about the past. But the legends agree on one thing. **In every version the person has the knowledge.** The trouble is what stands between knowledge and people: the magician turned it against people, the scientist towards himself, the keeper hid it from people, the frightened one from himself.

It is written in the cards too. Waite retells old interpretations in which the Hermit’s lantern holds “the Light of Occult Science” and his staff is “a Magic Wand”. And Benebell Wen sees in the Moon hidden abilities and resistance: what rises from the unconscious is kept out of consciousness “due to fear or hyperactive defense mechanisms”. Almost word for word, the legend of the frightened wizard.

Our reading: the wizard of this tail casts no spells. The gift is lunar — imagination, instinct, an eye for the hidden — and it stays locked in a tower of books and thought. The tower is the two Hermits standing before the Moon; they are the legendary “block”. For everyone with this tail a third Hermit holds the centre of the chart, the comfort zone, so the tail rarely feels like a problem — more like character.

report.h3: The brighter the lantern, the blacker the night

report: The Hermit has a lantern: his own, bright, obedient, and within its circle of a few steps everything is visible. The Moon’s light is reflected, dim and borrowed, but it lights the whole landscape: nothing is sharp, but the way can be seen. A person with 9-9-18 trusts only the lantern, but it cannot light the road the tail’s root points to. Waite calls it “the issue into the unknown”. The dog and the wolf beside it are “the fears of the natural mind” before the exit, “when there is only reflected light to guide it”.

The eye takes about forty minutes to adjust fully to the dark, and bright light knocks that adjustment out. That is why astronomers use dim red torches. Someone holding a bright lantern before their eyes sees almost nothing beyond its circle: the eyes are tuned to the lantern. **The brighter the light in the hand, the blacker the night around it.** The longer a person works things out alone, the scarier everything beyond the understood becomes — and the greater the need to work out more. Dim the lantern and wait, and road, trees and horizon emerge. Moonlight is enough.

The scene is invented. Vera has spent nine years studying psychology: a second degree, eleven certificates. A friend invites her to lead a meeting on anxiety. Vera replies: “I need to prepare.” This is not fright but the entry, the Hermit: anything unclear must first be understood alone. The course she buys opens three new questions, and the meeting slides to the autumn, then to “after New Year”. This is the mechanism, the Hermit again: the circle of light moves with her, and beyond its edge it is always dark. Waite insisted the Hermit is a card of attainment, not of quest. Vera already knows as much as a mentor, yet feels like an eternal student.

Meanwhile, beyond the circle, the Moon grows. Before sleep Vera runs through the meeting: a question she cannot answer, a smirk in the third row. Sometimes the dream turns the other way — the radio, a book of her own. Both dreams are the Moon, “life of the imagination apart from life of the spirit”, in Waite’s words. **In this tail fear is born not from what happened but from what never did.**

The meeting never took place. A year later the club invited an acquaintance with one introductory course, and she is already running her third group. “But she doesn’t really know anything” — here is the “intellectual vanity” attributed to the tail: not arrogance but defence. The acquaintance walked the road; Vera knows it from a map. And every year of preparation raises the price of the first step: “After ten years of study I can’t give a bad talk.”

report.h3: The gudgeon bathed in moonlight; Prospero broke his staff

report: Two old stories read as two endings of the tail; the parallels are ours. Saltykov-Shchedrin’s Wise Gudgeon, a fish with “a whole chamber of wits”, spent a year hollowing out a burrow “just the right size for one”. And then: “At night he took his exercise and bathed in the moonlight, and by day he climbed into his burrow and trembled.” Everything lunar is his — night, water, a crayfish at the burrow, a dream of a lottery win. Only the road is missing. Dying, he asks himself: “Whom had he comforted? To whom had he given good advice?” The answer: “To no one, no one.” The tale is extreme, but recognisable.

Prospero in Shakespeare’s “The Tempest” is a literal wizard. He lost his dukedom while buried in books: “my library / Was dukedom large enough.” For twelve years he rules an island of spirits and dreams from his cell, as he calls it. In the finale he breaks his staff — the very one old interpretations called a magic wand — and drowns his book. He keeps the knowledge and gives up control over every step. And he comes out to people: “Now my charms are all o’erthrown, / And what strength I have’s mine own, / Which is most faint.” This is the lunar road: sailing home, into the unknown, by whatever light there is.

report.h3: Dim the lantern, don’t discard it

report: No need to throw the lantern away: depth is these people’s real gift. Dimming it lets the eyes adjust to the moon. The practices follow from the roles of the cards; no ritual, no promises.

ul: Half an hour with “I don’t know”: no books, advice or internet; writing down what emerges — guesses, images, bodily sensations.
An “enough” threshold with a date: “After this course I lead my first meeting.” The Hermit will always find one more gap — let the threshold decide.
Naming the dog and the wolf: “I’m afraid I won’t cope”, “I’m afraid they’ll laugh at me” — and deciding what to do if it happens. A named fear howls but does not bite.

report: If fear, anxiety or solitude get in the way of sleeping, working and living, if for years not a single step gets taken, that is something to take to a psychologist or psychotherapist.

report.h3: A guide on the night road

report: The Moon, once walked through, gives what many clever people lack: the ability to act without full clarity and an imagination that creates rather than frightens. In Waite, the Hermit’s beacon intimates that “where I am, you also may be.” Only someone who knows the road can say that. Someone who never left the summit can give light but cannot lead the way. Someone who has walked the lunar road — with fear, to the howling of the dog and the wolf, by reflected light — knows where the potholes are. **The lived-through 9-9-18 is not a sage in a tower but a guide on the night road.** With such a guide, not knowing stops being frightening.
